Sendust is an alloy composed of 5% aluminum, 10% silicon, and 85% iron.
The composite consists of sendust and aluminum particles dispersed in polystyrene resin.
Aluminum particle sizes used were approximately 8 µm and 50 µm.
Sendust particle size was approximately 5 µm.
The frequency range studied was from 500 MHz to 40 GHz.
Return loss less than −20 dB corresponds to absorption of more than 99% of incident power.
The composite achieved return loss below −20 dB over several GHz and near 20 GHz.
Volume mixture ratios of sendust and aluminum were varied while keeping total volume constant.
Complex permeability µ* = µ' − jµ'' and permittivity ε* = ε' − jε'' were measured.
Eddy currents in aluminum particles contribute to the magnetic moment affecting µ''.
The composite was fabricated by mixing particles in polystyrene resin dissolved in acetone, then hot-pressing at 5 MPa.
Mass densities of composites ranged from 2.1 to 2.7 g/cm³, lighter than ferrite tiles (~5.0 g/cm³).
Frequency dependence of µ* can be controlled by adjusting aluminum particle size and volume mixture ratio.
The non-reflective condition relates µ* and ε* to minimize reflection and maximize absorption.
Measured ε' values varied slightly among composites (16 to 24), ε'' was almost constant.
Theoretical calculations of µ' and µ'' matched well with measured values for aluminum composites.
Increasing sendust volume increased µ' below 10 GHz and above 20 GHz.
Increasing sendust volume increased µ'' below 18 GHz but decreased it above 23 GHz.
Return loss was calculated for metal-backed single-layer absorbers with incident waves perpendicular to the surface.
Normalized −20 dB bandwidth was broader for composite with higher aluminum content.
